security_audit.summary: The static command and filesystem findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code, and tool names in a documentation-only skill. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, obfuscated code, or bundled executable malware. The main residual concern is guidance that recommends allowing all tools by default.

remediation.suggestion: Recommend least-privilege allowed-tools by default, and leave the field empty only when broad access is clearly required.

remediation.issue: Shell setup example lacks safety context
remediation.suggestion: State that directory creation commands should run only inside the intended project or skill workspace.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Tool Permission Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends leaving allowed-tools empty to allow all tools unless restriction is needed. This can cause generated skills to request unnecessary execution, file, and network capabilities.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance is explicit and repeated in the skill. It is not malicious, but it weakens least-privilege defaults for generated skills.

content.value_statement: AI skills need clear structure, reusable resources, and safe activation rules. This skill guides authors through planning, writing, testing, and packaging focused skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md metadata and the optional allowed-tools field.
Shows how to plan scripts, references, and assets from concrete examples.
Provides a six-step process for naming, creating, editing, testing, and packaging skills.
Includes a reusable SKILL.md template with sections for resources, examples, notes, and success criteria.
Compares skills with slash commands for workflow selection.
limitations: Does not include runnable helper scripts or validation tooling.
Focuses on Claude-style skill packaging and may need adaptation for other marketplaces.
Gives general guidance; it does not enforce least-privilege tool settings.
Requires users to supply domain examples, assets, and reference material.

use_cases.title: Design Internal Agent Skills
use_cases.description: Create focused skills that capture team workflows, reference material, and repeatable procedures.

use_cases.title: Standardize Skill Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn scattered process notes into structured SKILL.md files with clear resources and test cases.

use_cases.title: Prepare Shared Skill Packages
use_cases.description: Review skill structure, frontmatter, examples, and packaging before sharing with a team or marketplace.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning from a rough idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-skill to help me design a skill for [task]. Ask for the key examples first, then draft the SKILL.md outline.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate revision of a draft skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current skill and suggest improvements to metadata, resource structure, and test cases. Keep the changes focused.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Bundled Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for reusable scripts, references, and assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these workflows, decide which scripts, references, and assets belong in the skill. Explain the purpose of each resource.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Distribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill for packaging readiness, least-privilege tools, duplicate content, and test coverage before marketplace submission.

output_examples.input: I need a skill that helps analysts summarize customer interviews.
output_examples.output: A focused skill plan with activation wording, SKILL.md sections, likely reference files, and test prompts for interview summaries.

output_examples.input: My skill is too long and repeats reference content.
output_examples.output: A revision plan that moves detailed material into references, keeps core workflow steps in SKILL.md, and lists validation checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a skill package for sharing with my team.
output_examples.output: A packaging checklist covering frontmatter, paths, included resources, examples, and a final test cycle.

best_practices: Start with concrete user examples before writing reusable instructions.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed schemas or policies into references.
Use the smallest practical allowed-tools list for each skill.
anti_patterns: Creating one broad skill that covers unrelated workflows.
Storing large reference material directly in SKILL.md.
Leaving all tools available when the workflow only needs read-only access.

faq.question: Does this skill create files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples. File creation depends on the assistant tools available in the current environment.

faq.question: Can it help update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an update flow for improving metadata, resources, tests, and packaging.

faq.question: Which files are required for a skill?
faq.answer: A SKILL.md file is required. Scripts, references, and assets are optional resources.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.

faq.question: How should allowed-tools be handled?
faq.answer: Use least privilege. Allow only tools needed for the workflow, especially before publishing shared skills.

faq.question: Can it validate marketplace security?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and review questions, but it does not replace a security audit or schema validator.
